key_insight: Geometry-based fragmentation enables multiscale polymer representations without predefined chemical fragmentation rules.
engineering_relevance: Combining polymer sequence notation with 3D structural information can improve property prediction for materials screening.
method: Formulate fragmentation as a radius-constrained optimization inspired by k-center, with fragment count determined by the radius.
Vary the radius to construct multiscale fragments using largely geometric information.
Integrate fragment-based attention into a multimodal model combining p-SMILES and 3D conformations.
evidence_signal: Experiments on a benchmark polymer dataset show improved prediction accuracy for several properties when adding 3D conformational information; explainability analyses probe physical relevance.
watch_item: Practical performance may depend on conformer quality and fragmentation radius; the abstract does not quantify sensitivity to either.
paper_title: Towards Multiscale Molecular Representation Learning through Geometry-Based Fragmentation for Polymer Property Prediction
